svg.title: Chromatic aberration
svg.desc: (a) White light from a point passes through a single converging lens. Violet light is bent more than red, so it focuses closer to the lens (V) than red light does (R), and the colors spread into fans. (b) An achromatic doublet, a converging lens cemented to a weaker diverging lens of different glass, brings white light of all colors to one focus. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Scan the focal positions of different colors
The detector moves; focal positions do not. The doublet model matches red and violet but retains a
small secondary spectrum. Geometric spots, not Airy disks.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
